On 11/26/13, 1:22 AM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> On Tuesday, November 26, 2013, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>

I think that last sentence got garbled in the translation!

> I really don't like the idea of things that used to work
> being broken. At the same time, I took the point that
> I've been too eager to focus on the latest bug rather than
> the bigger picture.
>
>
> I think this one should be taken seriously. I don't like the idea of runs just hanging indefinitely. The process is
> still running on the windows box. If it's a concurrent I/o thing, it's fine and we need to figure out how to stop this
> behavior. If it's our command line hanging, that's not good.

No. But then neither are any other bugs.

It looks like it's configured for many iterations,
and if it's having trouble with the geometry, then it
could just be taking many leapfrog steps per iteration.

Are you sure it's not making any progress vs. just
taking a long time to do the large number of iterations
it's trying to do? If it does 1000 leapfrog steps/iteration,
that can be a lot of work for 10K iterations --- but then the
model's pretty simple.

- Bob
